decisions.reason: Although it builds on existing web-service capabilities, address autocomplete is a generic utility with limited fit to the firm's announced regulated-energy platform strategy and only modest visible commitment.

The Austrian gas grid fee database is close to the firm's core data business, uses sunk database and domain investments, and management can plausibly justify weak uptake as a niche-market ramp-up issue.
Peak load window determination is tightly aligned with the firm's compliance, calculation, and digitization offer, so prior investment and strategic fit make management likely to persist.

An end-customer tariff database with several models represents a visible product-line commitment and fits the firm's platform direction, which strongly favors continued support despite any early disappointment.

Custom web services are less standardized than the firm's SaaS ambition but still support broader end-to-end service provision, so escalation of commitment makes withdrawal less likely than continuation.
Postal code lookup is a low-differentiation add-on with weak centrality to the firm's regulated-energy positioning, so management is comparatively more willing to reallocate effort elsewhere.
